topics.label: Lecture introduction and course framing
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the students, outlines the structure and multidisciplinary scope of the course, and presents the day's learning outcomes.

topics.label: Cellular origin, genetic progression, and modeling of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer develops from accumulated genetic alterations that disrupt normal differentiation and tissue architecture, and how these processes are studied in culture.

topics.label: Tumor invasion, metastasis, and the benign-to-malignant transition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how tumors progress from contained benign lesions into invasive and metastatic malignancies using histological and clinical examples.

topics.label: Neoplasm nomenclature and classification conventions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the standard terminology and exceptions used to name benign and malignant tumors based on their tissue of origin.

topics.label: Pathophysiological mechanisms of cancer illness and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the direct physical and systemic mechanisms by which primary and metastatic tumors cause disease and death.

topics.label: Cancer incidence across human tissues and animal taxa
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics compare the occurrence and mortality rates of different tumor types in human populations and across diverse animal species.

topics.label: Clinical presentation and screening strategies for cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address the diagnostic challenges of early cancer symptoms and evaluate the effectiveness of screening programs for various cancer types.

topics.label: Conclusion and lecture review
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session by referencing the learning outcomes and providing logistical instructions for upcoming practicals and lectures.
